reusedOwner.semanticBoundary: A caller-supplied finite scalar is assigned to lower-inclusive ordered buckets; this fixture narrows the scalar to a nonnegative JSON integer data-packet count for one already-constructed TCP transfer and direction.

inputMeasure: caller-derived count of data packets in one direction of one already-constructed TCP transfer
inputBoundary: One caller-supplied nonnegative integer data-packet count. TCP transfer construction, uplink/downlink direction assignment, and classification of a packet as data rather than control traffic are established upstream.

canonicalSetting.sourceObservedSetting: performance.retransmission_threshold: direction has more than 10 data packets

settings.outputBoundary: Report only whether the supplied directional data-packet count belongs in the paper's retransmission-rate population. More than 10 is exactly at least 11 only at this integer boundary.

canonicalSetting.sourceObservedSetting: performance.throughput: TCP transfer throughput by direction for transfers with at least 10 data packets

settings.outputBoundary: Report only whether the supplied directional data-packet count belongs in the paper's throughput population. At least 10 includes equality.

limitations: The fixture does not construct TCP transfers, infer direction, or classify packets as data packets.
The output is population-boundary satisfaction; retransmission rate and throughput values are not computed.
No flow timeout, retransmission-identification rule, throughput unit, duration denominator, or missing-transfer policy is inferred.
The source has no released trace rows or analysis code, so this binding proves only the two disclosed packet-count predicates.
